findings.description: Guard-page probe claim is overstated in codegen_notes.md ('places every input and the output flush against a PROT_NONE page'). Reviewer layout dump shows the arrays form one contiguous slab placed top-down: only vb (placed first) ends flush at the guard page; every other array's overflow lands in the next array's mapped bytes, and out is the LOWEST array, so a write overflow past out would land in lup/gate region and cannot fault. The probe also checks no-fault only, not out contents.
findings.evidence: Reviewer placement dump (spot_checks.py section 5): vb end_rel_guard=+0 FLUSH-GUARD; out end_rel_guard=-43367. Mitigations that keep this low: the dominant OOB class (unmasked tail reads at pixel row B) faults on vb and the reviewer's negative control proved it does (rc=-10 both gangs); loads and stores derive from the same ISPC foreach mask; the 340-point size sweep bitwise-compares all valid outputs; input canaries cover write-to-input.
findings.recommendation: For the B7-40 integration review, re-place out first (flush at guard) and add an out-content check in the probe; fix the wording in codegen_notes.md.

findings.description: The chunked 4-thread schedule is a timing-script construct (timing_dev.py), not an adapter feature: it bypasses the guarded adapter (raw cached ctypes pointers, no validation, lifetimes held only by local Python references, no per-chunk failure isolation - a mid-chunk failure propagates through ThreadPoolExecutor.map with the output partially written). Legality of the schedule itself is sound: pixels are independent, chunks disjoint in inputs and output, shared tables read-only, kernel stateless with no ISPC tasking, ctypes CDLL releases the GIL. Bitwise equality is asserted after every chunked rep at exactly the timed B sizes (16384 and 65536). Author self-flagged this in proof_record notes (3).
findings.evidence: timing_dev.py:141-166; timing_log.json bitwise_check + in-rep assert; proof_record.md 'Independent verdict' note (3).
findings.recommendation: A threaded integration path must be implemented and re-reviewed in the adapter (validation per chunk or upfront on the full block, explicit buffer lifetime ownership, defined failure semantics) before any B7-40 use; dev-tier timing also runs A always first (not the protocol's frozen alternating order), so final numbers must follow B7-03 freeze with exclusive host lease.

scope: Approved: the C_native ISPC kernel (lw_primary.ispc, both neon-i32x4 and neon-i32x8 builds) as an exact port of the frozen longwave primary reducer graph for its admitted domain, its guarded single-thread ctypes adapter (lw_native.py) including pre-launch rejection, immutability, aliasing and B=0 behavior, and the shipped exactness/guard/FMA evidence for dev-tier selection use in B7-30 trials. Source-level typed-graph audit confirmed: two ordered patch sweeps; reflection depending only on A0+lup with f32 chain ((a0+lup)*factor*0.5/pi), pi from bits 0x40490FDB, hardware fdiv, no reciprocal; solar_gate true branch order A8,A7,A3,A2 / false branch A7,A2 with a real uniform branch; f64 surface chains with a single RN f32 rounding at the accumulator add (fcvtn) and f32 specialization staying f32; sky chains f32; sweep-2 cast-per-multiply grouping; ordered left-fold outputs 0/1 and copies 2..6; +0.0f accumulator init; lanes own independent pixels (no cross-lane reduction; no faddp anywhere). Not approved / not claimed by this review: an integrated multi-threaded chunked path (does not exist as adapter code), decision-grade performance numbers (dev-tier noisy-host paired reps only; B7-03 protocol trials with exclusive lease remain the authority), and packaging/portability beyond the local prototype.
recommended_disposition: Advance C_native (B7-20 ISPC) into the B7-30 A/B/C selection trials as an exact eligible candidate: exactness and guard evidence is reproducible and real (1040/1040 + 340 + 84 bitwise, 22/22 rejections, canaries clean, zero-FMA codegen independently rebuilt byte-identical), and the honest as-shipped cost statement (1T adapter loses to 4-thread numba, ~0.6x; kernel-level chunked 4T ~2.2x at B=65536) is supported by the logs with the F4 integration caveats. Apply F1-F3 doc/test touch-ups in the candidate's own follow-up (they do not block selection).
